en.title: Afghanistan: state formation, corridor dependence and the political economy of a landlocked society
en.deck: Afghanistan's post-2021 order sits on older constraints: fragmented geography, external-resource dependence, shallow formal finance, a narrow productive base and a young population whose productive potential is constrained by weak capital formation and restrictions on women and girls.
en.regime: Centralized de facto order over a low-income, import-dependent and financially shallow economy exposed to regional corridors, return migration and human-capital constraints.
en.key_risk: Population and returnee pressure, aid retrenchment, border disruption, climate stress and human-capital losses may outpace private investment and productive diversification.

pt-BR.title: Afeganistão: formação do Estado, dependência de corredores e economia política
pt-BR.deck: A ordem pós-2021 repousa sobre restrições antigas: geografia fragmentada, dependência de recursos externos, finanças formais rasas, base produtiva estreita e população jovem cujo potencial produtivo é limitado pela baixa formação de capital e pelas restrições impostas a mulheres e meninas.
pt-BR.regime: Ordem de facto centralizada sobre economia de baixa renda, importadora e financeiramente rasa, exposta a corredores regionais, migração de retorno e restrições de capital humano.
pt-BR.key_risk: Pressão populacional e de retornados, retração da ajuda, disrupção fronteiriça, clima e perdas de capital humano podem superar investimento e diversificação produtiva.

selection_rationale: The published post-2021 Strategic Transition establishes a material Afghanistan mechanism but focuses on the transition itself. Reusable context remains missing for state formation, corridor geography, productive structure, finance, demography, human capital, water and regional dependence.
contrary_evidence: Territorial consolidation and stronger revenue collection contradict a simple failed-state description.
Aggregate GDP recovery does not imply household recovery when population grows faster and per-capita output falls.
Opium suppression demonstrates enforcement capacity but not a replacement rural economy.
Exchange-rate stability does not establish normal financial intermediation.
Geological resources do not constitute operating industrial capacity.
limitations: No recent comprehensive census; population estimates change rapidly with mass returns.
International estimates use different periods and methods and should not be merged mechanically.
Fiscal, security and financial data are less transparent than in a normal statistical system.
Competing state claims on armed groups are attributed rather than treated as independently verified facts.
Planned infrastructure and announced mining projects are not treated as operating capacity.
